requirements.description: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) can help you with access permissions and authorizations by checking for IAM passwords and access keys that are not used for a specified time period.

requirements.name: CloudWatch should not allow cross-account sharing
requirements.description: Ensure that your AWS CloudWatch is configured to allow access only to friendly AWS accounts in order to prevent unauthorized users from sharing their CloudWatch events.

requirements.name: EC2 transit gateways should have auto accept shared attachments disabled
requirements.description: Ensure transit gateways have auto accept shared attachments feature disabled. If this setting is disabled, then any VPC that attempts to attach to a transit gateway will need to request authorization, and the account that owns the transit gateway will need to accept the authorization.

requirements.name: SNS topic policies should prohibit cross account access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring SNS topics does not have cross account access.

requirements.name: EC2 instance detailed monitoring should be enabled
requirements.description: Enable this rule to help improve AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instance monitoring on the AWS EC2 console, which displays monitoring graphs with a 1-minute period for the instance.

requirements.name: EC2 instances should be managed by AWS Systems Manager
requirements.description: An inventory of the software platforms and applications within the organization is possible by managing AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instances with AWS Systems Manager.

requirements.name: EC2 stopped instances should be removed in 30 days
requirements.description: Enable this rule to help with the baseline configuration of AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instances by checking whether AWS EC2 instances have been stopped for more than the allowed number of days, according to your organization's standards.

requirements.name: VPC EIPs should be associated with an EC2 instance or ENI
requirements.description: This rule ensures Elastic IPs allocated to a AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC) are attached to AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instances or in-use Elastic Network Interfaces.

requirements.name: VPC network access control lists (network ACLs) should be associated with a subnet.
requirements.description: Ensure there are no unused network access control lists (network ACLs). The rule is compliant if each network ACL is associated with a subnet. The rule is non-compliant if a network ACL is not associated with a subnet.

requirements.name: API Gateway stage logging should be enabled
requirements.description: API Gateway logging displays detailed views of users who accessed the API and the way they accessed the API.

requirements.name: At least one multi-region AWS CloudTrail should be present in an account
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail records AWS Management Console actions and API calls. You can identify which users and accounts called AWS, the source IP address from where the calls were made, and when the calls occurred. CloudTrail will deliver log files from all AWS Regions to your S3 bucket if MULTI_REGION_CLOUD_TRAIL_ENABLED is enabled.

requirements.name: At least one enabled trail should be present in a region
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail can help in non-repudiation by recording AWS Management Console actions and API calls. You can identify the users and AWS accounts that called an AWS service, the source IP address where the calls generated, and the timings of the calls. Details of captured data are seen within AWS CloudTrail Record Contents.

requirements.name: ELB application and classic load balancer logging should be enabled
requirements.description: Elastic Load Balancing activity is a central point of communication within an environment.

requirements.name: Redshift cluster audit logging and encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: To protect data at rest, ensure that encryption is enabled for your AWS Redshift clusters. You must also ensure that required configurations are deployed on AWS Redshift clusters. The audit logging should be enabled to provide information about connections and user activities in the database.

requirements.name: S3 bucket logging should be enabled
requirements.description: AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) server access logging provides a method to monitor the network for potential cybersecurity events.

requirements.name: VPC flow logs should be enabled
requirements.description: The VPC flow logs provide detailed records for information about the IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in your AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC.

requirements.name: Auto Scaling groups with a load balancer should use health checks
requirements.description: The Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) health checks for AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) Auto Scaling groups support maintenance of adequate capacity and availability.

requirements.name: DynamoDB table auto scaling should be enabled
requirements.description: AWS DynamoDB auto scaling uses the AWS Application Auto Scaling service to adjust provisioned throughput capacity that automatically responds to actual traffic patterns.

requirements.name: DynamoDB tables should be in a backup plan
requirements.description: To help with data back-up processes, ensure your AWS DynamoDB tables are a part of an AWS Backup plan.

requirements.name: DynamoDB table point-in-time recovery should be enabled
requirements.description: Enable this rule to check that information has been backed up. It also maintains the backups by ensuring that point-in-time recovery is enabled in AWS DynamoDB.

requirements.name: RDS Aurora clusters should be protected by backup plan
requirements.description: Checks if AWS Aurora DB clusters are protected by a backup plan. The rule is non-compliant if the AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) Database Cluster is not protected by a backup plan.

requirements.name: RDS DB instance backup should be enabled
requirements.description: The backup feature of AWS RDS creates backups of your databases and transaction logs.

requirements.name: RDS DB instances should be in a backup plan
requirements.description: To help with data back-up processes, ensure your AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances are a part of an AWS Backup plan.

requirements.name: S3 bucket cross-region replication should be enabled
requirements.description: AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) Cross-Region Replication (CRR) supports maintaining adequate capacity and availability.

requirements.name: S3 buckets should have lifecycle policies configured
requirements.description: This control checks if AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets have lifecycle policy configured. This rule fails if AWS S3 lifecycle policy is not enabled.

requirements.name: S3 bucket object lock should be enabled
requirements.description: Ensure that your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) bucket has lock enabled, by default.

requirements.name: S3 buckets with versioning enabled should have lifecycle policies configured
requirements.description: This control checks if AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) version enabled buckets have lifecycle policy configured. This rule fails if AWS S3 lifecycle policy is not enabled.

requirements.name: S3 bucket versioning should be enabled
requirements.description: AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) bucket versioning helps keep multiple variants of an object in the same AWS S3 bucket.

requirements.name: Backup plan min frequency and min retention check
requirements.description: Checks if a backup plan has a backup rule that satisfies the required frequency and retention period(35 Days). The rule is non-compliant if recovery points are not created at least as often as the specified frequency or expire before the specified period.

requirements.name: Backup recovery points should be encrypted
requirements.description: Ensure that a recovery point is encrypted. The rule is non-compliant if the recovery point is not encrypted.

requirements.name: Backup recovery points manual deletion should be disabled
requirements.description: Checks if a backup vault has an attached resource-based policy which prevents deletion of recovery points. The rule is non-compliant if the Backup Vault does not have resource-based policies or has policies without a suitable 'Deny' statement.

requirements.name: Backup recovery points should not expire before retention period
requirements.description: Ensure a recovery point expires no earlier than after the specified period. The rule is non-compliant if the recovery point has a retention point less than 35 days.

requirements.name: DynamoDB table should be protected by backup plan
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS DynamoDB tables are protected by a backup plan. The rule is non-compliant if the DynamoDB Table is not covered by a backup plan.

requirements.name: EBS volumes should be in a backup plan
requirements.description: To help with data back-up processes, ensure your AWS Elastic Block Store (AWS EBS) volumes are a part of an AWS Backup plan.

requirements.name: EBS volumes should be protected by a backup plan
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS Elastic Block Store (AWS EBS) volumes are protected by a backup plan. The rule is non-compliant if the AWS EBS volume is not covered by a backup plan.

requirements.name: EC2 instances should be protected by backup plan
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instances are protected by a backup plan. The rule is non-compliant if the AWS EC2 instance is not covered by a backup plan.

requirements.name: EFS file systems should be in a backup plan
requirements.description: To help with data back-up processes, ensure your AWS Elastic File System (AWS EFS) file systems are a part of an AWS Backup plan.

requirements.name: EFS file systems should be protected by backup plan
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS Elastic File System (AWS EFS) File Systems are protected by a backup plan. The rule is non-compliant if the EFS File System is not covered by a backup plan.

requirements.name: ElastiCache Redis cluster automatic backup should be enabled with retention period of 15 days or greater
requirements.description: When automatic backups are enabled, AWS ElastiCache creates a backup of the cluster on a daily basis. The backup can be retained for a number of days as specified by your organization. Automatic backups can help guard against data loss.

requirements.name: ELB application load balancer deletion protection should be enabled
requirements.description: This rule ensures that Elastic Load Balancing has deletion protection enabled.

requirements.name: FSx file system should be protected by backup plan
requirements.description: Checks if AWS FSx File Systems are protected by a backup plan. The rule is non-compliant if the AWS FSx File System is not covered by a backup plan.

requirements.name: RDS DB instance should be protected by backup plan
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances are protected by a backup plan. The rule is non-compliant if the AWS RDS Database instance is not covered by a backup plan.

requirements.name: EC2 instances high level findings should not be there in inspector scans
requirements.description: AWS Inspector scans operating system packages installed on your AWS EC2 instances for vulnerabilities and network reachability issues. Each finding has the name of the detected vulnerability and provides a severity rating, information about the affected resource, and details such as how to remediate the reported vulnerability.

manual_reasons: Rejected as an automatic predicate only: the exact question needs operator judgement or data outside the read-only per-scope snapshot. Preserved as a manual attestation with source and framework mappings.

requirements.name: ECR repositories should have image scan on push enabled
requirements.description: Ensure AWS Elastic Container Registry (ECR) repositories have image scanning enabled. The rule is non-compliant if image scanning is not enabled for the ECR repository.

requirements.name: AWS Security Hub should be enabled for an AWS Account
requirements.description: AWS Security Hub helps to monitor unauthorized personnel, connections, devices, and software. AWS Security Hub aggregates, organizes, and prioritizes the security alerts, or findings, from multiple AWS services.

requirements.name: GuardDuty should be enabled
requirements.description: AWS GuardDuty can help to monitor and detect potential cybersecurity events by using threat intelligence feeds.

requirements.name: RDS DB instance and cluster enhanced monitoring should be enabled
requirements.description: Enable AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) to help monitor AWS RDS availability. This provides detailed visibility into the health of your AWS RDS database instances.

requirements.name: Ensure the S3 bucket CloudTrail logs to is not publicly accessible
requirements.description: CloudTrail logs a record of every API call made in your account. These log files are stored in an S3 bucket. Security Hub recommends that the S3 bucket policy, or access control list (ACL), be applied to the S3 bucket that CloudTrail logs to prevent public access to the CloudTrail logs.

requirements.name: CloudTrail trails should be enabled in all regions
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail is a web service that records AWS API calls for your account and delivers log files to you. The recorded information includes the identity of the API caller, the time of the API call, the source IP address of the API caller, the request parameters, and the response elements returned by the AWS service. CloudTrail provides a history of AWS API calls for an account, including API calls made via the Management Console, SDKs, command line tools, and higher-level AWS services (such as CloudFormation).

requirements.name: Ensure S3 bucket access logging is enabled on the CloudTrail S3 bucket
requirements.description: S3 Bucket Access Logging generates a log that contains access records for each request made to your S3 bucket. An access log record contains details about the request, such as the request type, the resources specified in the request worked, and the time and date the request was processed. It is recommended that bucket access logging be enabled on the CloudTrail S3 bucket.

requirements.name: CloudTrail trails should be integrated with CloudWatch logs
requirements.description: Use AWS CloudWatch to centrally collect and manage log event activity. Inclusion of AWS CloudTrail data provides details of API call activity within your AWS account.

requirements.name: CloudTrail trail logs should be encrypted with KMS CMK
requirements.description: To help protect sensitive data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS CloudWatch Log Groups.

requirements.name: CloudTrail trail log file validation should be enabled
requirements.description: Utilize AWS CloudTrail log file validation to check the integrity of CloudTrail logs. Log file validation helps determine if a log file was modified or deleted or unchanged after CloudTrail delivered it. This feature is built using industry standard algorithms: SHA-256 for hashing and SHA-256 with RSA for digital signing. This makes it computationally infeasible to modify, delete or forge CloudTrail log files without detection.

requirements.name: CloudWatch alarm should have an action configured
requirements.description: Checks if CloudWatch alarms have an action configured for the ALARM, INSUFFICIENT_DATA, or OK state. Optionally checks if any actions match a named ARN. The rule is non-compliant if there is no action specified for the alarm or optional parameter.

requirements.name: AWS Config should be enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether AWS Config is enabled in the account for the local Region and is recording all resources.

requirements.name: KMS CMK rotation should be enabled
requirements.description: Enable key rotation to ensure that keys are rotated once they have reached the end of their crypto period.

requirements.name: Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for S3 bucket policy changes
requirements.description: You can do real-time monitoring of API calls by directing CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. Security Hub recommends that you create a metric filter and alarm for changes to S3 bucket policies. Monitoring these changes might reduce time to detect and correct permissive policies on sensitive S3 buckets.

requirements.name: Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for CloudTrail configuration changes
requirements.description: You can do real-time monitoring of API calls by directing CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. Security Hub recommends that you create a metric filter and alarm for changes to CloudTrail configuration settings. Monitoring these changes helps ensure sustained visibility to activities in the account.

requirements.name: Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for AWS Config configuration changes
requirements.description: You can do real-time monitoring of API calls by directing CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. Security Hub recommends that you create a metric filter and alarm for changes to AWS Config configuration settings. Monitoring these changes helps ensure sustained visibility of configuration items in the account

requirements.name: Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for AWS Management Console authentication failures
requirements.description: You can do real-time monitoring of API calls by directing CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. Security Hub recommends that you create a metric filter and alarm for failed console authentication attempts.

requirements.name: Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for AWS Management Console sign-in without MFA
requirements.description: You can do real-time monitoring of API calls by directing CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. Security Hub recommends that you create a metric filter and alarm console logins that aren't protected by MFA.

requirements.name: Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for disabling or scheduled deletion of customer managed keys
requirements.description: You can do real-time monitoring of API calls by directing CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. Security Hub recommends that you create a metric filter and alarm for customer managed keys that have changed state to disabled or scheduled deletion. Data encrypted with disabled or deleted keys is no longer accessible.

requirements.name: Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for IAM policy changes
requirements.description: You can do real-time monitoring of API calls by directing CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. Security Hub recommends that you create a metric filter and alarm for changes made to IAM policies. Monitoring these changes helps ensure that authentication and authorization controls remain intact.

requirements.name: Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for changes to Network Access Control Lists (NACL)
requirements.description: You can do real-time monitoring of API calls by directing CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. NACLs are used as a stateless packet filter to control ingress and egress traffic for subnets in a VPC. Security Hub recommends that you create a metric filter and alarm for changes to NACLs. Monitoring these changes helps ensure that AWS resources and services aren't unintentionally exposed.

requirements.name: Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for changes to network gateways
requirements.description: You can do real-time monitoring of API calls by directing CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. Network gateways are required to send and receive traffic to a destination outside a VPC. Security Hub recommends that you create a metric filter and alarm for changes to network gateways.

requirements.name: Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for usage of 'root' account
requirements.description: You can do real-time monitoring of API calls directing CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms.Security Hub recommends that you create a metric filter and alarm for root login attempts. Monitoring for root account logins provides visibility into the use of a fully privileged account and an opportunity to reduce the use of it.

requirements.name: Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for route table changes
requirements.description: You can do real-time monitoring of API calls by directing CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. Routing tables route network traffic between subnets and to network gateways. Security Hub recommends that you create a metric filter and alarm for changes to route tables. Monitoring these changes helps ensure that all VPC traffic flows through an expected path.

requirements.name: Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for security group changes
requirements.description: You can do real-time monitoring of API calls by directing CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. Security groups are a stateful packet filter that controls ingress and egress traffic in a VPC. Security Hub recommends that you create a metric filter and alarm for changes to security groups. Monitoring these changes helps ensure that resources and services aren't unintentionally exposed.

requirements.name: Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for unauthorized API calls
requirements.description: Real-time monitoring of API calls can be achieved by directing CloudTrail Logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. It is recommended that a metric filter and alarm be established for unauthorized API calls.

requirements.name: Ensure a log metric filter and alarm exist for VPC changes
requirements.description: You can do real-time monitoring of API calls by directing CloudTrail logs to CloudWatch Logs and establishing corresponding metric filters and alarms. You can have more than one VPC in an account, and you can create a peer connection between two VPCs, enabling network traffic to route between VPCs. Security Hub recommends that you create a metric filter and alarm for changes to VPCs.

requirements.name: Ensure Images (AMI's) are encrypted
requirements.description: Amazon Machine Images should utilize EBS Encrypted snapshots.

requirements.name: IAM unattached custom policy should not have statements with admin access
requirements.description: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) can help you incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties with access permissions and authorizations, restricting policies from containing 'Effect': 'Allow' with 'Action': '*' over 'Resource': '*'.

requirements.name: Ensure inline policies attached to IAM users, roles, and groups should not allow blocked actions on KMS keys
requirements.description: Checks if the inline policies attached to IAM users, roles, and groups do not allow blocked actions on all AWS Key Management Service (KMS) keys. The rule is non - compliant if any blocked action is allowed on all KMS keys in an inline policy.

requirements.name: IAM root user hardware MFA should be enabled
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring hardware MFA is enabled for the root user.

requirements.name: IAM root user MFA should be enabled
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring MFA is enabled for the root user.

requirements.name: IAM user access keys should be rotated at least every 90 days
requirements.description: The credentials are audited for authorized devices, users, and processes by ensuring IAM access keys are rotated as per organizational policy.

requirements.name: Ensure IAM users with access keys unused for 45 days or greater are disabled
requirements.description: AWS IAM users can access AWS resources using access keys. It is recommended that access keys that have been unused in 45 or greater days be deactivated or removed.

requirements.name: IAM administrator users should have MFA enabled
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring MFA is enabled for users with administrative privileges.

requirements.name: ACM certificates should not expire within 30 days
requirements.description: Ensure network integrity is protected by ensuring X509 certificates are issued by AWS ACM.

requirements.name: Ensure that ACM certificates are not in failed state
requirements.description: This control ensures that ACM certificates are not in failed state.

requirements.name: Ensure that ACM certificates are not in pending validation state
requirements.description: This control ensures that ACM certificates are not in pending validation state. When certificates are not validated within 72 hours after the request is made, those certificates become invalid.

requirements.name: Ensure that all the expired ACM certificates are removed
requirements.description: This control ensures that all expired ACM certificates are removed from AWS account.

requirements.name: RSA certificates managed by ACM should use a key length of at least 2,048 bits
requirements.description: This control checks whether RSA certificates managed by AWS Certificate Manager use a key length of at least 2,048 bits. The control fails if the key length is smaller than 2,048 bits.

requirements.name: ACM certificates should have transparency logging enabled
requirements.description: Ensure ACM certificates transparency logging is enabled as certificate transparency logging guards against SSL/TLS certificates issued by mistake or by a compromised certificate authority.

requirements.name: KMS CMK policies should prohibit public access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring AWS KMS CMK cannot be publicly accessed.

requirements.name: KMS key decryption should be restricted in IAM customer managed policy
requirements.description: Checks whether the default version of IAM customer managed policies allow principals to use the AWS KMS decryption actions on all resources. This control uses Zelkova, an automated reasoning engine, to validate and warn you about policies that may grant broad access to your secrets across AWS accounts. This control fails if the kms:Decrypt or kms:ReEncryptFrom actions are allowed on all KMS keys. The control evaluates both attached and unattached customer managed policies. It does not check inline policies or AWS managed policies.

requirements.name: KMS key decryption should be restricted in IAM inline policy
requirements.description: Checks whether the inline policies that are embedded in your IAM identities (role, user, or group) allow the AWS KMS decryption actions on all KMS keys. This control uses Zelkova, an automated reasoning engine, to validate and warn you about policies that may grant broad access to your secrets across AWS accounts. This control fails if kms:Decrypt or kms:ReEncryptFrom actions are allowed on all KMS keys in an inline policy.

requirements.name: Athena workgroups should be encrypted at rest
requirements.description: This control checks if an Athena workgroup is encrypted at rest. The control fails if an Athena workgroup isn't encrypted at rest.

requirements.name: Attached EBS volumes should have encryption enabled
requirements.description: Because sensitive data can exist and to help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Elastic Block Store (AWS EBS) volumes.

requirements.name: EBS encryption by default should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure that encryption is enabled for your AWS Elastic Block Store (AWS EBS) volumes.

requirements.name: EBS snapshots should be encrypted
requirements.description: Ensure that EBS snapshots are encrypted. This rule is non-compliant if the EBS snapshot is not encrypted.

requirements.name: EBS volume encryption at rest should be enabled
requirements.description: Because sensitive data can exist and to help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Elastic Block Store (AWS EBS) volumes.

requirements.name: ECS clusters encryption at rest should be enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether ECS Clustes have encryption at rest enabled. The check fails if encryption at rest is not enabled as sensitive data should be protected.

requirements.name: EFS file system encryption at rest should be enabled
requirements.description: Because sensitive data can exist and to help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Elastic File System (EFS).

requirements.name: EFS file systems should be encrypted with CMK
requirements.description: Ensure AWS Elastic File Systems (AWS EFS) are encrypted using CMK. The rule is non-compliant if the EFS File System is not encrypted using CMK.

requirements.name: Neptune DB clusters should be encrypted at rest
requirements.description: This control checks whether a Neptune DB cluster is encrypted at rest. The control fails if a Neptune DB cluster isn't encrypted at rest.

requirements.name: Neptune DB cluster snapshots should be encrypted at rest
requirements.description: This control checks whether a Neptune DB cluster snapshot is encrypted at rest. The control fails if a Neptune DB cluster isn't encrypted at rest.

requirements.name: RDS DB clusters should be encrypted at rest
requirements.description: This control checks if an RDS DB cluster is encrypted at rest. The control fails if an RDS DB cluster isn't encrypted at rest.

requirements.name: RDS DB instance encryption at rest should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure that encryption is enabled for your AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances.

requirements.name: S3 bucket default encryption should be enabled with KMS
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets.

requirements.name: S3 bucket default encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets.

requirements.name: S3 buckets should enforce SSL
requirements.description: To help protect data in transit, ensure that your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets require requests to use Secure Socket Layer (SSL).

requirements.name: SNS topics should be encrypted at rest
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure that your AWS Simple Notification Service (AWS SNS) topics require encryption using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).

requirements.name: AWS SQS queues should be encrypted at rest
requirements.description: This control checks whether AWS SQS queues are encrypted at rest.

requirements.name: SQS queues should be encrypted with KMS CMK
requirements.description: To help protect sensitive data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS SQS queues with KMS CMK.

requirements.name: SSM parameters encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: This control checks if SSM parameter has encryption enabled.

requirements.name: CloudFront distributions should use custom SSL/TLS certificates
requirements.description: This control checks whether CloudFront distributions are using the default SSL/TLS certificate CloudFront provides. This control passes if the CloudFront distribution uses a custom SSL/TLS certificate. This control fails if the CloudFront distribution uses the default SSL/TLS certificate.

requirements.name: Directory Service certificates should not expire within 90 days
requirements.description: Is is recommended to monitor certificate expiration and implement automated alerts to notify the responsible team for timely certificate replacement or removal.

requirements.name: EFS file systems should enforce SSL
requirements.description: To help protect data in transit, ensure that your EFS file systems require requests to use Secure Socket Layer (SSL).

requirements.name: ELB application and network load balancers should only use SSL or HTTPS listeners
requirements.description: Ensure that Application Load Balancers and Network Load Balancers are configured to use certificates from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). This rule is compliant if at least 1 load balancer is configured without a certificate from ACM.

requirements.name: ELB classic load balancers should use SSL certificates
requirements.description: Because sensitive data can exist and to help protect data at transit, ensure encryption is enabled for your Elastic Load Balancing.

requirements.name: ELB classic load balancers should only use SSL or HTTPS listeners
requirements.description: Ensure that your Elastic Load Balancers (ELBs) are configured with SSL or HTTPS listeners. Because sensitive data can exist, enable encryption in transit to help protect that data.

requirements.name: ELB listeners should use secure SSL cipher
requirements.description: Ensure that ELB listeners do not have any insecure SSL ciphers. Using insecure and deprecated ciphers for your ELB Predefined Security Policy or Custom Security Policy could make the SSL connection between the client and the load balancer vulnerable to exploits.

requirements.name: ELB network load balancers should have TLS listener security policy configured
requirements.description: Ensure that your Network Load Balancers (NLBs) are configured with a TLS listener security policy. Using insecure ciphers for your NLB Predefined or Custom Security Policy could make the TLS connection between the client and the load balancer vulnerable to exploits.

requirements.name: ELB listeners SSL/TLS protocol version should be checked
requirements.description: Using insecure ciphers for your ELB Predefined or Custom Security Policy, could make the SSL connection between the client and the load balancer vulnerable to exploits. TLS 1.0 was recommended to be disabled by PCI Council after June 30, 2016.

requirements.name: EMR clusters encryption in transit should be enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether EMR clusters have encryption in transit enabled. This control fails if an EMR cluster isn't encrypted in transit.

requirements.name: Connections to Elasticsearch domains should be encrypted using TLS 1.2
requirements.description: This control checks whether connections to Elasticsearch domains are required to use TLS 1.2. The check fails if the Elasticsearch domain TLSSecurityPolicy is not Policy-Min-TLS-1-2-2019-07.

requirements.name: MSK clusters should be encrypted in transit among broker nodes
requirements.description: This controls checks if an Amazon MSK cluster is encrypted in transit with HTTPS (TLS) among the broker nodes of the cluster. The control fails if plain text communication is enabled for a cluster broker node connection.

requirements.name: OpenSearch domains node-to-node encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: This control checks if AWS OpenSearch Service nodes are encrypted end to end. The rule is non-compliant if the node-to-node encryption is not enabled on the domain.

requirements.name: Redshift cluster encryption in transit should be enabled
requirements.description: Ensure that your AWS Redshift clusters require TLS/SSL encryption to connect to SQL clients.

requirements.name: Backup plan should exist in a region
requirements.description: Ensure that there exists at least one backup plan in a region. The rule is non-compliant if there are no backup plans in a region.

requirements.name: Backup report plan should exist in a region where backup plan is enabled
requirements.description: Ensure that there is a minimum of one backup report plan in each region. The rule will be considered non-compliant if a region with backup plans does not have any backup report plans.

requirements.name: Backup vaults should exist in a region
requirements.description: Ensure that there exists at least one backup vault in a region. The rule is non-compliant if there are no backup vaults in a region.

requirements.name: Neptune DB clusters should have automated backups enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether a Neptune DB cluster has automated backups enabled, and a backup retention period greater than or equal to 7 days. The control fails if backups aren't enabled for the Neptune DB cluster, or if the retention period is less than 7 days.

requirements.name: Neptune DB clusters should be configured to copy tags to snapshots
requirements.description: This control checks if a Neptune DB cluster is configured to copy all tags to snapshots when the snapshots are created. The control fails if a Neptune DB cluster isn't configured to copy tags to snapshots.

requirements.name: Directory Service directories manual snapshots limit should not be less than 2
requirements.description: Ensure you keep track of the number of manual snapshots for your monitor to guarantee sufficient capacity when it becomes necessary.

requirements.name: DLM EBS snapshot lifecycle policy should be enabled
requirements.description: Ensure DLM EBS snapshot lifecycle policy is enabled in all the regions with EBS snapshots.

requirements.name: Network Firewall policies should have at least one rule group associated
requirements.description: This control checks whether a Network Firewall policy has any stateful or stateless rule groups associated. The control fails if stateless or stateful rule groups are not assigned.

requirements.name: Stateless network firewall rule group should not be empty
requirements.description: A rule group contains rules that define how your firewall processes traffic in your VPC. An empty stateless rule group when present in a firewall policy might give the impression that the rule group will process traffic. However, when the stateless rule group is empty, it does not process traffic.

requirements.name: Secrets Manager secrets should be rotated within a specified number of days
requirements.description: This control checks whether your secrets have been rotated at least once within 90 days. Rotating secrets can help you to reduce the risk of an unauthorized use of your secrets in your AWS account. Examples include database credentials, passwords, third-party API keys, and even arbitrary text. If you do not change your secrets for a long period of time, the secrets are more likely to be compromised.

requirements.name: Auto Scaling groups should not have any suspended processes
requirements.description: Ensure that there are no Auto Scaling Groups (ASGs) with suspended processes provisioned in your AWS account in order to avoid disrupting the auto scaling workflow.

requirements.name: AWS Redshift should have automatic upgrades to major versions enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether automatic major version upgrades are enabled for the AWS Redshift cluster.

requirements.name: AWS Redshift should have required maintenance settings
requirements.description: Ensure whether AWS Redshift clusters have the specified maintenance settings. Redshift clusters `allowVersionUpgrade` should be set to `true` and `automatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod` should be greater than 7.

requirements.name: DRS jobs should be enabled
requirements.description: Ensure that DRS is enabled with jobs. This rule is non-compliant if DRS is not enabled with jobs for a particular region.

requirements.name: Attached EBS volumes should have delete on termination enabled
requirements.description: This rule ensures that AWS Elastic Block Store volumes that are attached to AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instances are marked for deletion when an instance is terminated.

requirements.name: EBS volume snapshots should exist
requirements.description: Ensure that EBS volume snapshots exist. This rule is non-compliant if the EBS volume does not have any snapshot.

requirements.name: EBS volumes should be attached to EC2 instances
requirements.description: Checks if EBS volumes are attached to EC2 instances.

requirements.name: AppSync graphql API logging should be enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether an AWS AppSync API has field-level logging turned on. The control fails if the field resolver log level is set to None. Unless you provide custom parameter values to indicate that a specific log type should be enabled, Security Hub produces a passed finding if the field resolver log level is either ERROR or ALL.

requirements.name: CloudFront distributions access logs should be enabled
requirements.description: This control checks if AWS CloudFront distributions are configured to capture information from AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) server access logs. This rule is non-compliant if a CloudFront distribution does not have logging configured.

requirements.name: Log group retention period should be at least 365 days
requirements.description: Ensure a minimum duration of event log data is retained for your log groups to help with troubleshooting and forensics investigations.

requirements.name: CodeBuild projects should have logging enabled
requirements.description: This control checks if an AWS CodeBuild project environment has at least one log option enabled. The rule is non-compliant if the status of all present log configurations is set to 'DISABLED'.

requirements.name: CodeBuild project S3 logs should be encrypted
requirements.description: This control checks if S3 logs for a CodeBuild project are encrypted. The control fails if encryption is deactivated for S3 logs for a CodeBuild project.

requirements.name: ECS task definitions should have logging enabled
requirements.description: Ensure logging is enabled for task definitions so that you can access your containerized application logs for debugging and auditing purposes. On top of centralized logging, these log drivers often include additional capabilities that are useful for operation.

requirements.name: Elastic Beanstalk environments should have enhanced health reporting enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment is configured to send logs to CloudWatch Logs. The control fails if the environment isn't configured to send logs to CloudWatch Logs.

requirements.name: Elasticsearch domains should have audit logging enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether Elasticsearch domains have audit logging enabled. This control fails if an Elasticsearch domain does not have audit logging enabled.

requirements.name: Elasticsearch domain error logging to CloudWatch Logs should be enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether Elasticsearch domains are configured to send error logs to CloudWatch Logs.

requirements.name: Elasticsearch domain should send logs to CloudWatch
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS OpenSearch Service (OpenSearch Service) domains are configured to send logs to AWS CloudWatch Logs. The rule is compliant if a log is enabled for an OpenSearch Service domain. This rule is non-compliant if logging is not configured.

requirements.name: Log group encryption at rest should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect sensitive data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS CloudWatch Log Group.

requirements.name: Neptune DB clusters should publish audit logs to CloudWatch Logs
requirements.description: This control checks whether a Neptune DB cluster publishes audit logs to AWS CloudWatch Logs. The control fails if a Neptune DB cluster doesn't publish audit logs to CloudWatch Logs. EnableCloudWatchLogsExport should be set to Audit.

requirements.name: Network Firewall logging should be enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether logging is enabled for an AWS Network Firewall firewall. The control fails if logging isn't enabled for at least one log type or if the logging destination doesn't exist.

requirements.name: Route 53 zones should have query logging enabled
requirements.description: Ensure Route 53 zones have query logging enabled.

requirements.name: S3 buckets object logging should be enabled
requirements.description: Object-Level logging saves events in JSON format in CloudTrail. This is recommended from a security best practice perspective for buckets that contain sensitive data.

requirements.name: EC2 auto scaling group launch configurations user data should not have any sensitive data
requirements.description: Ensure that sensitive information is not included in the user data of the launch configuration. It is recommended to utilize Secrets Manager as an alternative for securely managing sensitive data.

rejected_reasons: Upstream runs a secret-content scanner over the decoded payload (detect-secrets / Kingfisher or substring and password-regex matching). PEASO is a read-only configuration CSPM that does not collect or scan secret material; the collector deliberately discards user data, environment values, commands and option values, and collecting them to grep for credentials is intrusive and unsuitable for the snapshot.

requirements.name: ECS containers should run as non-privileged
requirements.description: This control checks if the privileged parameter in the container definition of AWS ECS Task Definitions is set to true. The control fails if this parameter is equal to true.

requirements.name: ECS containers should be limited to read-only access to root filesystems
requirements.description: This control checks if ECS containers are limited to read-only access to mounted root filesystems. This control fails if the ReadonlyRootFilesystem parameter in the container definition of ECS task definitions is set to false.

requirements.name: ECS task definitions should not share the host's process namespace
requirements.description: This control checks if AWS ECS task definitions are configured to share a host's process namespace with its containers. The control fails if the task definition shares the host's process namespace with the containers running on it.

requirements.name: ECS task definitions should not use root user.
requirements.description: This control checks if ECS task definitions have root user. This control fails if the ECS task definitions have root user.

requirements.name: ECS task definition container definitions should be checked for host mode
requirements.description: Check if AWS Elastic Container Service (AWS ECS) task definition with host networking mode has 'privileged' or 'user' container definitions.The rule is non-compliant for task definitions with host network mode and container definitions of privileged=false or empty and user=root or empty.

requirements.name: ECR repositories should have lifecycle policies configured
requirements.description: This control checks if ECR repositories have lifecycle policy configured. This rule fails if ECR repository lifecycle policy is not enabled.

requirements.name: ECR repositories should prohibit public access
requirements.description: Ensure there are no ECR repositories set as public.

requirements.name: ECR private repositories should have tag immutability configured
requirements.description: This control checks whether a private ECR repository has tag immutability enabled. This control fails if a private ECR repository has tag immutability disabled. This rule passes if tag immutability is enabled and has the value IMMUTABLE.

requirements.name: ECS task definition containers should not have secrets passed as environment variables
requirements.description: This control checks if the key value of any variables in the environment parameter of container definitions includes AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, or ECS_ENGINE_AUTH_DATA. This control fails if a single environment variable in any container definition equals AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, or ECS_ENGINE_AUTH_DATA. This control does not cover environmental variables passed in from other locations such as AWS S3.

requirements.name: Networkfirewall firewall should be in a VPC
requirements.description: Deploy AWS Networkfirewall firewall within an AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC) for a secure communication between a function and other services within the AWS VPC.

requirements.name: The default stateless action for Network Firewall policies should be drop or forward for fragmented packets
requirements.description: This control checks whether the default stateless action for fragmented packets for a Network Firewall policy is drop or forward. The control passes if Drop or Forward is selected, and fails if Pass is selected.

requirements.name: The default stateless action for Network Firewall policies should be drop or forward for full packets
requirements.description: A firewall policy defines how your firewall monitors and handles traffic in AWS VPC. You configure stateless and stateful rule groups to filter packets and traffic flows. Defaulting to Pass can allow unintended traffic.

requirements.name: SNS topic policies should prohibit public access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring AWS SNS topics cannot be publicly accessed.

requirements.name: SNS topic policies should prohibit publishing access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring SNS topics cannot be accessed publicly for publishing.

requirements.name: SNS topic policies should prohibit subscription public access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring SNS topics cannot be accessed publicly for subscription.

requirements.name: VPC should be configured to use VPC endpoints
requirements.description: Checks if Service Endpoint for the service provided in rule parameter is created for each AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC). The rule is non-compliant if an AWS VPC doesn't have an AWS VPC endpoint created for the service.

requirements.name: VPC default security group should not allow inbound and outbound traffic
requirements.description: AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) security groups can help in the management of network access by providing stateful filtering of ingress and egress network traffic to AWS resources.

requirements.name: VPC security groups should restrict ingress access on ports 20, 21, 22, 3306, 3389, 4333 from 0.0.0.0/0
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring common ports are restricted on AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) security groups.

requirements.name: VPC security groups should restrict ingress SSH access from 0.0.0.0/0
requirements.description: AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) Security Groups can help manage network access by providing stateful filtering of ingress and egress network traffic to AWS resources.

requirements.name: VPC security groups should restrict ingress TCP and UDP access from 0.0.0.0/0
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring common ports are restricted on AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) Security Groups.

requirements.name: EC2 auto scaling groups should cover multiple availability zones
requirements.description: This control checks whether an AWS EC2 Auto Scaling group spans multiple availability zones. The control fails if an auto scaling group does not span multiple availability zones.

requirements.name: AWS Redshift enhanced VPC routing should be enabled
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS Redshift cluster has 'enhancedVpcRouting' enabled. The rule is non-compliant if 'enhancedVpcRouting' is not enabled or if the configuration.enhancedVpcRouting field is 'false'.

requirements.name: Neptune DB clusters should have deletion protection enabled
requirements.description: This control checks if a Neptune DB cluster has deletion protection enabled. The control fails if a Neptune DB cluster doesn't have deletion protection enabled.

requirements.name: AWS Redshift clusters should have automatic snapshots enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether AWS Redshift clusters have automated snapshots enabled. It also checks whether the snapshot retention period is greater than or equal to seven.

requirements.name: Ensure EC2 Auto Scaling Groups Propagate Tags to EC2 Instances that it launches
requirements.description: Tags can help with managing, identifying, organizing, searching for, and filtering resources. Additionally, tags can help with security and compliance. Tags can be propagated from an Auto Scaling group to the EC2 instances that it launches.

requirements.name: EC2 Auto Scaling groups should use EC2 launch templates
requirements.description: This control checks whether an AWS EC2 Auto Scaling group is created from an EC2 launch template. This control fails if an AWS EC2 Auto Scaling group is not created with a launch template or if a launch template is not specified in a mixed instances policy.

requirements.name: CloudWatch alarm action should be enabled
requirements.description: Checks if AWS CloudWatch alarm actions are in enabled state. The rule is non-compliant if the CloudWatch alarm actions are not in enabled state.

requirements.name: RDS DB instance multiple az should be enabled
requirements.description: Multi-AZ support in AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) provides enhanced availability and durability for database instances.

requirements.name: Logging of delivery status should be enabled for notification messages sent to a topic
requirements.description: This control checks whether logging is enabled for the delivery status of notification messages sent to an AWS SNS topic for the endpoints. This control fails if the delivery status notification for messages is not enabled.

requirements.name: GuardDuty findings should be archived
requirements.description: AWS GuardDuty helps you understand the impact of an incident by classifying findings by severity: low, medium, and high.

requirements.name: GuardDuty Detector should not have high severity findings
requirements.description: GuardDuty generates a finding whenever it detects unexpected and potentially malicious activity in your AWS environment. If critical findings are not addressed threats can spread in the environment. This rule is non-compliant if there are high severity findings.

requirements.name: CloudFormation stacks should have notifications enabled
requirements.description: Ensure CloudFormation stacks are associated with an SNS topic to receive notifications when an event occurs.

requirements.name: IAM Security Audit role should be created to conduct security audits
requirements.description: Ensure IAM Security Audit role is created. By creating an IAM role with a security audit policy, a distinct segregation of responsibilities is established between the security team and other teams within the organization.

requirements.name: Ensure a support role has been created to manage incidents with AWS Support
requirements.description: AWS provides a support center that can be used for incident notification and response, as well as technical support and customer services.

requirements.name: S3 buckets should have event notifications enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether S3 Event Notifications are enabled on an AWS S3 bucket. This control fails if S3 Event Notifications are not enabled on a bucket.

requirements.name: RDS clusters should have deletion protection enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether RDS clusters have deletion protection enabled. This control is intended for RDS DB instances. However, it can also generate findings for Aurora DB instances, Neptune DB instances, and AWS DocumentDB clusters. If these findings are not useful,then you can suppress them.

requirements.name: RDS DB clusters should be configured for multiple Availability Zones
requirements.description: This control checks whether high availability is enabled for your RDS DB clusters. RDS DB clusters should be configured for multiple Availability Zones to ensure availability of the data that is stored.

requirements.name: RDS DB instances should have deletion protection enabled
requirements.description: Ensure AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances have deletion protection enabled.

requirements.name: S3 public access should be blocked at account level
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets cannot be publicly accessed.

requirements.name: ACM certificates should not expire within 30 days
requirements.description: Ensure network integrity is protected by ensuring X509 certificates are issued by AWS ACM.

requirements.name: API Gateway stage should uses SSL certificate
requirements.description: Ensure that a REST API stage uses a Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) certificate. This rule is compliant if the REST API stage does not have an associated SSL certificate.

requirements.name: API Gateway stage cache encryption at rest should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your API Gateway stage's cache.

requirements.name: Auto Scaling groups with a load balancer should use health checks
requirements.description: The Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) health checks for AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) Auto Scaling groups support maintenance of adequate capacity and availability.

requirements.name: Auto Scaling launch config public IP should be disabled
requirements.description: Ensure that AWS EC2 Auto Scaling groups have public IP addresses enabled through Launch Configurations. This rule is non-compliant if the Launch Configuration for an Auto Scaling group has AssociatePublicIpAddress set to 'true'.

requirements.name: Backup recovery points should be encrypted
requirements.description: Ensure that a recovery point is encrypted. The rule is non-compliant if the recovery point is not encrypted.

requirements.name: CloudTrail trail logs should be encrypted with KMS CMK
requirements.description: To help protect sensitive data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS CloudWatch Log Groups.

requirements.name: CloudTrail trail log file validation should be enabled
requirements.description: Utilize AWS CloudTrail log file validation to check the integrity of CloudTrail logs. Log file validation helps determine if a log file was modified or deleted or unchanged after CloudTrail delivered it. This feature is built using industry standard algorithms: SHA-256 for hashing and SHA-256 with RSA for digital signing. This makes it computationally infeasible to modify, delete or forge CloudTrail log files without detection.

requirements.name: CodeBuild project artifact encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: This control checks if a CodeBuild project has encryption enabled for all of its artifacts. The rule is non-compliant if 'encryptionDisabled' is set to 'true' for any primary or secondary (if present) artifact configurations.

requirements.name: DynamoDB table auto scaling should be enabled
requirements.description: AWS DynamoDB auto scaling uses the AWS Application Auto Scaling service to adjust provisioned throughput capacity that automatically responds to actual traffic patterns.

requirements.name: DynamoDB table should be encrypted with AWS KMS
requirements.description: Ensure that encryption is enabled for your AWS DynamoDB tables. Because sensitive data can exist at rest in these tables, enable encryption at rest to help protect that data.

requirements.name: Attached EBS volumes should have encryption enabled
requirements.description: Because sensitive data can exist and to help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Elastic Block Store (AWS EBS) volumes.

requirements.name: EBS encryption by default should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure that encryption is enabled for your AWS Elastic Block Store (AWS EBS) volumes.

requirements.name: EC2 instance detailed monitoring should be enabled
requirements.description: Enable this rule to help improve AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instance monitoring on the AWS EC2 console, which displays monitoring graphs with a 1-minute period for the instance.

requirements.name: EFS file system encryption at rest should be enabled
requirements.description: Because sensitive data can exist and to help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Elastic File System (EFS).

requirements.name: Elastic Beanstalk enhanced health reporting should be enabled
requirements.description: AWS Elastic Beanstalk enhanced health reporting enables a more rapid response to changes in the health of the underlying infrastructure. These changes could result in a lack of availability of the application. Elastic Beanstalk enhanced health reporting provides a status descriptor to gauge the severity of the identified issues and identify possible causes to investigate.

requirements.name: ELB application load balancer deletion protection should be enabled
requirements.description: This rule ensures that Elastic Load Balancing has deletion protection enabled.

requirements.name: Application Load Balancer should be configured to drop invalid http headers
requirements.description: Ensure that your Elastic Load Balancers (ELB) are configured to drop invalid http header.

requirements.name: ELB application load balancers should redirect HTTP requests to HTTPS
requirements.description: To help protect data in transit, ensure that your Application Load Balancer automatically redirects unencrypted HTTP requests to HTTPS.

requirements.name: ELB application and network load balancers should only use SSL or HTTPS listeners
requirements.description: Ensure that Application Load Balancers and Network Load Balancers are configured to use certificates from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). This rule is compliant if at least 1 load balancer is configured without a certificate from ACM.

requirements.name: ELB classic load balancers should have cross-zone load balancing enabled
requirements.description: Enable cross-zone load balancing for your Elastic Load Balancers (ELBs) to help maintain adequate capacity and availability. The cross-zone load balancing reduces the need to maintain equivalent numbers of instances in each enabled availability zone.

requirements.name: ELB classic load balancers should use SSL certificates
requirements.description: Because sensitive data can exist and to help protect data at transit, ensure encryption is enabled for your Elastic Load Balancing.

requirements.name: ELB classic load balancers should only use SSL or HTTPS listeners
requirements.description: Ensure that your Elastic Load Balancers (ELBs) are configured with SSL or HTTPS listeners. Because sensitive data can exist, enable encryption in transit to help protect that data.

requirements.name: ES domain encryption at rest should be enabled
requirements.description: Because sensitive data can exist and to help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Elasticsearch Service (AWS ES) domains.

requirements.name: Elasticsearch domain node-to-node encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: Ensure node-to-node encryption for AWS Elasticsearch Service is enabled. Node-to-node encryption enables TLS 1.2 encryption for all communications within the AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC).

requirements.name: Kinesis streams should have server side encryption enabled
requirements.description: Enable server side encryption (SSE) of your AWS Kinesis Server data at rest, in order to protect your data and metadata from breaches or unauthorized access, and fulfill compliance requirements for data-at-rest encryption within your organization.

requirements.name: Log group encryption at rest should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect sensitive data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS CloudWatch Log Group.

requirements.name: OpenSearch domains should have encryption at rest enabled
requirements.description: This control checks whether AWS OpenSearch domains have encryption-at-rest configuration enabled. The check fails if encryption at rest is not enabled.

requirements.name: OpenSearch domains node-to-node encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: This control checks if AWS OpenSearch Service nodes are encrypted end to end. The rule is non-compliant if the node-to-node encryption is not enabled on the domain.

requirements.name: RDS DB instances should have deletion protection enabled
requirements.description: Ensure AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances have deletion protection enabled.

requirements.name: RDS DB instance encryption at rest should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure that encryption is enabled for your AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances.

requirements.name: RDS DB instance multiple az should be enabled
requirements.description: Multi-AZ support in AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) provides enhanced availability and durability for database instances.

requirements.name: RDS DB snapshots should be encrypted at rest
requirements.description: Ensure that encryption is enabled for your AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) snapshots.

requirements.name: Redshift cluster encryption in transit should be enabled
requirements.description: Ensure that your AWS Redshift clusters require TLS/SSL encryption to connect to SQL clients.

requirements.name: Redshift cluster audit logging and encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: To protect data at rest, ensure that encryption is enabled for your AWS Redshift clusters. You must also ensure that required configurations are deployed on AWS Redshift clusters. The audit logging should be enabled to provide information about connections and user activities in the database.

requirements.name: S3 bucket default encryption should be enabled with KMS
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets.

requirements.name: S3 bucket default encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption is enabled for your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets.

requirements.name: S3 buckets should enforce SSL
requirements.description: To help protect data in transit, ensure that your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets require requests to use Secure Socket Layer (SSL).

requirements.name: S3 bucket object lock should be enabled
requirements.description: Ensure that your AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) bucket has lock enabled, by default.

requirements.name: S3 public access should be blocked at account level
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets cannot be publicly accessed.

requirements.name: SageMaker endpoint configuration encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) is enabled for your SageMaker endpoint.

requirements.name: SageMaker notebook instance encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) is enabled for your SageMaker notebook.

requirements.name: SNS topics should be encrypted at rest
requirements.description: To help protect data at rest, ensure that your AWS Simple Notification Service (AWS SNS) topics require encryption using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).

requirements.name: SSM documents should not be public
requirements.description: This control checks whether AWS Systems Manager documents that are owned by the account are public. This control fails if SSM documents with the owner Self are public.

requirements.name: Both VPN tunnels provided by AWS Site-to-Site VPN should be in UP status
requirements.description: Redundant Site-to-Site VPN tunnels can be implemented to achieve resilience requirements.

requirements.name: API Gateway stage should be associated with WAF
requirements.description: Ensure that an AWS API Gateway API stage is using a WAF Web ACL. This rule is non-compliant if an AWS WAF Web ACL is not used.

requirements.name: DMS replication instances should not be publicly accessible
requirements.description: Manage access to the AWS Cloud by ensuring DMS replication instances cannot be publicly accessed.

requirements.name: EBS snapshots should not be publicly restorable
requirements.description: Manage access to the AWS Cloud by ensuring EBS snapshots are not publicly restorable.

requirements.name: EC2 instances should be in a VPC
requirements.description: Deploy AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instances within an AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC) to enable secure communication between an instance and other services within the amazon VPC, without requiring an internet gateway, NAT device, or VPN connection.

requirements.name: EC2 instances should not have a public IP address
requirements.description: Manage access to the AWS Cloud by ensuring AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instances cannot be publicly accessed.

requirements.name: EC2 instances should use IMDSv2
requirements.description: Ensure the Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2) method is enabled to help protect access and control of AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) instance metadata.

requirements.name: ELB application load balancers should have Web Application Firewall (WAF) enabled
requirements.description: Ensure AWS WAF is enabled on Elastic Load Balancers (ELB) to help protect web applications.

requirements.name: EMR cluster Kerberos should be enabled
requirements.description: The access permissions and authorizations can be managed and incorporated with the principles of least privilege and separation of duties, by enabling Kerberos for AWS EMR clusters.

requirements.name: EMR cluster master nodes should not have public IP addresses
requirements.description: Manage access to the AWS Cloud by ensuring AWS EMR cluster master nodes cannot be publicly accessed.

requirements.name: ES domains should be in a VPC
requirements.description: Manage access to the AWS Cloud by ensuring AWS Elasticsearch Service (AWS ES) Domains are within an AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC).

requirements.name: IAM password policies for users should have strong configurations
requirements.description: The identities and the credentials are issued, managed, and verified based on an organizational IAM password policy.

requirements.name: IAM groups should have at least one user
requirements.description: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) can help you incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties with access permissions and authorizations, by ensuring that IAM groups have at least one IAM user.

requirements.name: IAM policy should not have statements with admin access
requirements.description: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) can help you incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties with access permissions and authorizations, restricting policies from containing 'Effect': 'Allow' with 'Action': '*' over 'Resource': '*'.

requirements.name: IAM root user hardware MFA should be enabled
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring hardware MFA is enabled for the root user.

requirements.name: IAM root user MFA should be enabled
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring MFA is enabled for the root user.

requirements.name: IAM root user should not have access keys
requirements.description: Access to systems and assets can be controlled by checking that the root user does not have access keys attached to their AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role.

requirements.name: IAM users with console access should have MFA enabled
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that MFA is enabled for all AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) users that have a console password.

requirements.name: IAM users should be in at least one group
requirements.description: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) can help you restrict access permissions and authorizations, by ensuring IAM users are members of at least one group.

requirements.name: IAM user MFA should be enabled
requirements.description: Enable this rule to restrict access to resources in the AWS Cloud.

requirements.name: IAM user should not have any inline or attached policies
requirements.description: This rule ensures AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies are attached only to groups or roles to control access to systems and assets.

requirements.name: Ensure IAM policies are attached only to groups or roles
requirements.description: By default, IAM users, groups, and roles have no access to AWS resources. IAM policies are the means by which privileges are granted to users, groups, or roles. It is recommended that IAM policies be applied directly to groups and roles but not users.

requirements.name: Lambda functions should be in a VPC
requirements.description: Deploy AWS Lambda functions within an AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC) for a secure communication between a function and other services within the AWS VPC.

requirements.name: Lambda functions should restrict public access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring AWS Lambda functions cannot be publicly accessed.

requirements.name: OpenSearch domains should be in a VPC
requirements.description: This control checks whether AWS OpenSearch domains are in a VPC. It does not evaluate the VPC subnet routing configuration to determine public access.

requirements.name: RDS DB instances should prohibit public access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances are not public.

requirements.name: RDS snapshots should prohibit public access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS Relational Database Service (AWS RDS) instances are not public.

requirements.name: Redshift clusters should prohibit public access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS Redshift clusters are not public.

requirements.name: S3 bucket policy should prohibit public access
requirements.description: This control checks that the access granted by the S3 bucket is restricted by any of the principals, federated users, service principals, IP addresses, or VPCs that you provide. The rule is compliant if a bucket policy is not present.

requirements.name: S3 buckets should prohibit public read access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by only allowing authorized users, processes, and devices access to AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets.

requirements.name: S3 buckets should prohibit public write access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by only allowing authorized users, processes, and devices access to AWS Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) buckets.

requirements.name: SageMaker notebook instances should not have direct internet access
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that AWS SageMaker notebooks do not allow direct internet access.

requirements.name: VPC default security group should not allow inbound and outbound traffic
requirements.description: AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) security groups can help in the management of network access by providing stateful filtering of ingress and egress network traffic to AWS resources.

requirements.name: VPC internet gateways should be attached to authorized vpc
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring that internet gateways are only attached to authorized AWS Virtual Private Cloud (AWS VPC).

requirements.name: VPC route table should restrict public access to IGW
requirements.description: Ensure that there are public routes in the route table to an Internet Gateway (IGW). The rule is non-compliant if a route to an IGW has a destination CIDR block of '0.0.0.0/0' or '::/0'.

requirements.name: VPC Security groups should only allow unrestricted incoming traffic for authorized ports
requirements.description: This control checks whether the VPC security groups that are in use allow unrestricted incoming traffic. Optionally the rule checks whether the port numbers are listed in the authorizedTcpPorts parameter. The default values for authorizedTcpPorts are 80 and 443.

requirements.name: VPC security groups should restrict ingress access on ports 20, 21, 22, 3306, 3389, 4333 from 0.0.0.0/0
requirements.description: Manage access to resources in the AWS Cloud by ensuring common ports are restricted on AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) security groups.

requirements.name: VPC security groups should restrict ingress SSH access from 0.0.0.0/0
requirements.description: AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (AWS EC2) Security Groups can help manage network access by providing stateful filtering of ingress and egress network traffic to AWS resources.

requirements.name: API Gateway stage logging should be enabled
requirements.description: API Gateway logging displays detailed views of users who accessed the API and the way they accessed the API.

requirements.name: At least one multi-region AWS CloudTrail should be present in an account
requirements.description: AWS CloudTrail records AWS Management Console actions and API calls. You can identify which users and accounts called AWS, the source IP address from where the calls were made, and when the calls occurred. CloudTrail will deliver log files from all AWS Regions to your S3 bucket if MULTI_REGION_CLOUD_TRAIL_ENABLED is enabled.

requirements.name: All S3 buckets should log S3 data events in CloudTrail
requirements.description: The collection of Simple Storage Service (AWS S3) data events helps in detecting any anomalous activity. The details include AWS account information that accessed an AWS S3 bucket, IP address, and time of event.

requirements.name: CloudTrail trails should be integrated with CloudWatch logs
requirements.description: Use AWS CloudWatch to centrally collect and manage log event activity. Inclusion of AWS CloudTrail data provides details of API call activity within your AWS account.

requirements.name: CodeBuild projects should have logging enabled
requirements.description: This control checks if an AWS CodeBuild project environment has at least one log option enabled. The rule is non-compliant if the status of all present log configurations is set to 'DISABLED'.
